entry.title: Welcome to My New Blog
entry.content:
I’m excited to launch this new blog space! After years of using Twitter, I wanted a platform where I could share my thoughts, research updates, and insights about machine learning, automotive technology, and formal verification without the constraints of a 280-character limit.

What to Expect

This blog will be a place where I share:

  • Deep dives into AI/ML topics - Especially around formal verification of neural networks
  • Company updates from roboGaze - Our journey in automotive ML
  • Technical articles - Code, algorithms, and best practices
  • Personal reflections - On technology, science, and innovation

Why Leave Twitter?

While Twitter was great for quick updates and networking, I felt the need for a more controlled, personal space where I can:

  1. Share longer-form content
  2. Include detailed images and diagrams
  3. Maintain a permanent archive of my thoughts
  4. Own my content completely

What’s Next?

I’ll be posting regularly about:

  • The latest developments in formal verification
  • Automotive AI safety standards (ASPICE, ASIL)
  • Conference talks and presentations
  • Interesting papers and research

Stay tuned for more content! You can still find me on LinkedIn and GitHub for professional updates.

entry.title: Formal Verification: The Future of Safe AI

link.title: Formal Verification: The Future of Safe AI

entry.content:
As we deploy machine learning models in safety-critical applications like autonomous vehicles, the question of verification becomes paramount. How can we prove that a neural network will behave correctly in all situations?

The Challenge

Traditional software can be tested exhaustively in many cases. But neural networks are different:

  • They learn from data, not explicit programming
  • Their behavior emerges from millions of parameters
  • Testing every possible input is impossible
  • Edge cases can have catastrophic consequences

Formal Verification as a Solution

Formal verification offers mathematical proofs of correctness. For neural networks, this means:

Proving properties like:

  • Output ranges for given input ranges
  • Robustness against adversarial perturbations
  • Consistency across similar inputs

Using techniques such as:

  • Abstract interpretation
  • SMT solving
  • Interval analysis
  • Symbolic execution

Why This Matters for Automotive

In automotive applications, we must comply with standards like ASPICE and ASIL. These require:

  1. Documented safety analysis
  2. Proof of correct behavior
  3. Traceable requirements
  4. Verification evidence

Formal verification provides the mathematical foundation for these requirements.

The Path Forward

At roboGaze, we’re pioneering the integration of formal verification into the ML development pipeline. This isn’t just academic research—it’s becoming a practical necessity for deploying AI in safety-critical systems.

The future of AI safety isn’t about hoping our models work correctly. It’s about proving they do.

entry.title: Budapest ML Conference 2024 - Key Takeaways
entry.content:
Last week, I had the privilege of presenting at the Budapest ML Conference 2024. The energy and innovation in the Hungarian ML community continue to impress me!

My Talk: Formal Verification of Neural Networks

I presented our work on formal verification techniques for neural networks in automotive applications. The main points covered:

  • Current challenges in ML verification
  • Mathematical foundations of formal methods
  • Practical applications in autonomous vehicles
  • Integration with ASPICE/ASIL workflows

The audience was highly engaged, with excellent questions about scalability and real-world deployment challenges.

Other Highlights

Synthetic Data Generation Panel The panel on synthetic data was fascinating. As someone working with data collection for automotive ML, I found the discussions about:

  • Quality vs. quantity trade-offs
  • Domain gap challenges
  • Validation strategies

Networking

Connected with amazing researchers and practitioners from:

  • BME (Budapest University of Technology)
  • Local startups
  • International companies with Hungarian offices

Reflections

The Budapest ML scene is thriving. It’s exciting to see so much talent and innovation coming from Hungary. Our work at roboGaze is part of this broader ecosystem of excellence.

Looking forward to next year’s conference!

Check out the conference website for more information and other talks.
